summary: 1830 is a long, intensely cerebral game of building rail networks while simultaneously manipulating a stock market, where the real game is knowing when to dump a company's stock on other players before running it into the ground. There is no luck at all — every outcome flows from player decisions, and the interplay between operating trains for revenue and gaming share prices is what makes it a genre-defining classic.
praised: Deep, purely skill-based strategy with zero randomness
The stock market / share manipulation layer is considered one of the best ever designed
High replayability due to emergent, player-driven outcomes
Satisfying long-term planning and tension between personal and company interests
criticised: Steep learning curve and high rules overhead for new players
Analysis paralysis, especially with more players
Can be brutal/'take that' via the robber baron stock mechanics, which some find mean-spirited
Not beginner friendly compared to lighter 18xx entries

interaction.kind: stock manipulation, route blocking, and negotiation

scoring.why: The winner is whoever ends the game with the greatest personal net worth, combining cash on hand and the value of their stock holdings.
